name: Monport GM Pro 50W Fiber
tagline: Integrated 50W fiber with autofocus: deeper metal engraving at a low price
tldr: The GM Pro 50W puts a 50W MAX source in Monport's integrated fiber chassis, with one-touch autofocus, electric lift and a 150 × 150 mm field. Monport lists 1.1 mJ of pulse energy and 0.10 mm maximum marking depth, enough for deep logos, 3D relief in several passes and thin-sheet cut-outs. $2,498 on Monport's store in October 2026, about $700 less than the split GT 50W ($3,199).
mainObjective: Deep metal engraving and faster marking on a compact bench fiber

priceRange.note: Official Monport store, Oct 2026: $2,498 machine only, $2,648 with rotary axis, $2,698 with LightBurn Pro

engraveExample.description: Filled logo on stainless steel plate

cutExample.description: Not a sheet cutter: thin metal only, in many passes

cannot: Clear glass or acrylic marking (needs UV or CO₂)
Parts larger than the 150 × 150 mm field without repositioning

pros: 1.1 mJ pulse energy and 0.10 mm listed depth: noticeably faster on deep logos and relief
About $700 less than Monport's split GT 50W ($3,199), with autofocus and electric lift kept (Monport store, Oct 2026)
Lightest tier of the line at 15.6 kg, easy to move between benches
cons: Same 150 × 150 mm field as the cheaper tier: the extra power buys depth, not area
Fixed-pulse MAX source: no controlled colour marking
Monport's comparison table appears to mislabel this tier's pulse and frequency figures, so check them with support

faq.question: What does the GM Pro 50W add over the 30W?
faq.answer: Pulse energy (1.1 mJ vs 0.78 mJ) and listed marking depth (0.10 mm vs 0.08 mm), for $498 more in October 2026. Field, autofocus, chassis and software are the same, so the 50W makes sense when deep engraving, relief or thin-metal cut-outs are a regular job.

faq.question: GM Pro 50W or Gweike G2 50W?
faq.answer: Both are integrated 50W fibers at about $2,500. The GM Pro 50W brings one-touch autofocus and Monport's US support; compare field options, software (the GM Pro runs BslAppSimple and LightBurn) and current bundles before choosing.

faq.question: Can the GM Pro 50W cut metal?
faq.answer: Thin sheet only, in many passes: Monport shows thin-sheet cutting among its uses, but it remains a marking laser with a 150 × 150 mm field, not a sheet cutter.

standoutFeatures.title: Depth for the money
standoutFeatures.body: 1.1 mJ of pulse energy and a 0.10 mm listed depth at $2,498: deep logos, gun and knife parts and 3D relief come within reach without split-fiber prices.

standoutFeatures.title: Compact and light
standoutFeatures.body: 15.6 kg on a 40 × 33 cm base, with autofocus and electric lift: a machine that moves to a market stall or a second bench without a cart.

beginnerNotes: This profile is the 50W tier of the GM Pro, the one to pick when engraving depth matters. Compare the other tiers via the chips.
proTips: For deep relief, alternate hatch angles between passes and refocus every few passes with the autofocus as the surface goes down. Keep fume extraction running: deep engraving produces far more metal dust than marking.

editorialDepth.advantages: The GM Pro 50W is the value pick of the line: deeper engraving and shorter jobs for a modest premium, in a compact chassis that keeps autofocus.
editorialDepth.limitations: The field stays at 150 × 150 mm, there is no colour marking, and the open galvo needs an enclosure or strict eye protection. Specs are Monport's until independent tests arrive.
